title: The Ascension and Matthias Chosen

questions.question: To whom does Luke address the book of Acts?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:1 (ESV): "In the first book, O Theophilus, I have dealt with all that Jesus began to do and teach,"

questions.question: For how many days after His resurrection did Jesus appear to His apostles and speak about the kingdom of God?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:3 (ESV): "He presented himself alive to them after his suffering by many proofs, appearing to them during forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God."

questions.question: What did Jesus command the apostles to wait for in Jerusalem?
options: The promise of the Father — the baptism of the Holy Spirit
The return of Elijah from heaven
A sign from the sun and moon
questions.correctAnswer: The promise of the Father — the baptism of the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Acts 1:4-5 (ESV): "he ordered them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father... you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days from now."

questions.question: When the apostles asked if Jesus would restore the kingdom to Israel at this time, what was His reply?
options: "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by his own authority."
"The kingdom will come only after you preach to all nations."
"The kingdom is already within you, seek it there."
"I will restore it after the Spirit comes upon you."
questions.correctAnswer: "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by his own authority."
questions.explanation: Acts 1:7 (ESV): "He said to them, 'It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by his own authority.'"

questions.question: "But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to..."?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:8 (ESV): "But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth."

questions.question: After Jesus was lifted up and a cloud took Him out of sight, who stood beside the apostles?
options: An angel with a flaming sword
questions.explanation: Acts 1:10 (ESV): "And while they were gazing into heaven as he went, behold, two men stood by them in white robes,"

questions.question: What did the two men in white robes say about Jesus' return?
options: "This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven."
"Go to Jerusalem and wait for the Spirit before he returns."
"He will return when every nation has heard the gospel."
"The Father alone knows when he will return to earth."
questions.correctAnswer: "This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven."
questions.explanation: Acts 1:11 (ESV): "This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven."

questions.question: From which mountain did Jesus ascend into heaven?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:12 (ESV): "Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's journey away."

questions.question: How did Judas Iscariot die, according to Peter's account in Acts 1?
options: He fell headlong, his body burst open and all his intestines gushed out
He hanged himself from a tree
He was struck dead by lightning
He drowned in the Sea of Galilee
questions.correctAnswer: He fell headlong, his body burst open and all his intestines gushed out
questions.explanation: Acts 1:18 (ESV): "Now this man acquired a field with the reward of his wickedness, and falling headlong he burst open in the middle and all his bowels gushed out."

questions.question: The field bought with Judas' money was called Akeldama. What does that name mean?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:19 (ESV): "...so that the field was called in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood."

questions.question: What were the qualifications for the man chosen to replace Judas as an apostle?
options: He must have accompanied them from John's baptism until the day Jesus was taken up, so he could be a witness to the resurrection
He must have been one of the seventy-two sent out by Jesus
He must have been from the tribe of Levi and be at least thirty years old
He must have seen one of the post-resurrection appearances and spoken in tongues
questions.correctAnswer: He must have accompanied them from John's baptism until the day Jesus was taken up, so he could be a witness to the resurrection
questions.explanation: Acts 1:21-22 (ESV): "So one of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day when he was taken up from us—one of these men must become with us a witness to his resurrection."

questions.question: Two men were put forward as candidates to replace Judas. Who were they?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:23 (ESV): "And they put forward two, Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias."

questions.question: How was the replacement for Judas ultimately chosen between the two candidates?
options: They cast lots and the lot fell on Matthias
The Holy Spirit spoke audibly and named Matthias
The eleven apostles voted unanimously for Matthias
Peter prayed and then pointed to Matthias
questions.correctAnswer: They cast lots and the lot fell on Matthias
questions.explanation: Acts 1:26 (ESV): "And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles."

questions.question: Approximately how many were gathered together in the upper room before Pentecost?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:15 (ESV): "In those days Peter stood up among the brothers (the company of persons was in all about 120)..."

questions.question: Peter quoted from Psalm 69 and Psalm 109 regarding Judas. What did the first quote say should happen to his place?
options: "Let his homestead become desolate, and let there be no one to dwell in it."
"Let his name be blotted out from the book of the living."
"Let his portion be given to another generation."
"Let his wickedness be remembered eternally before God."
questions.correctAnswer: "Let his homestead become desolate, and let there be no one to dwell in it."
questions.explanation: Acts 1:20 (ESV): "For it is written in the Book of Psalms, 'Let his camp become desolate, and let there be no one to dwell in it'; and 'Let another take his office.'"

key_verse_text: "But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth."
